claims.head: Strength vs. Strength
claims.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Predators are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Blues’ chance quality wins out.
claims.call: The Blues’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Predators.
claims.nums: St. Louis 1st for chance quality (a 7.1% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Nashville 8th for preventing dangerous shots

chips.tip: St. Louis: a 7.1% chance of scoring on the average shot, 1st of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 7 and 7 games this season.
Nashville: a 6.1% chance of scoring on the average shot against, 8th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 7 and 7 games this season.

claims.head: Top line on top line: O'Reilly vs. Thomas
claims.call: The Predators’ L1 (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot) spends at least 53% of its 5-on-5 time against the Blues’ first line, against about 34% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blues’ first line is Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud.
claims.nums: At home: 72% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 34% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Andrew Brunette likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Blues’ first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Nashville home games this season · 4 games, 41 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 34% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: The Blues should drive the play
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Blues have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Blues’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
claims.call: The Blues get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

claims.gist: The Blues usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.

NSH.head: The Predators start a half-step behind
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage, St. Louis has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ best way to tip it is a penalty kill that holds up.

STL.head: The Blues start a half-step ahead
